text:
alex: FYI saw a short window of stale kv reads after a prefix handback in canary #7.

devon: logs?

alex: snippet: 2025-02-14T11:12:05Z prefix-handoff tenant=acme prefix=org:123 handback_epoch=42 observed_epoch=40 WARN kv-read value_stale=true

maria: Likely cause: visibility epoch not durable or token cached without revalidate.

sam: Do we persist a visible_epoch today?

alex: No, epoch is implicit in lease tokens; distributed best-effort. Explains short divergence.

jing: Options: make visible_epoch durable (CAS), add generation-id + cheap revalidate, or accept repair window with background fixes.

devon: CAS is clean but adds writes on handback. How bad would that be under rebalance?

alex: Spikes could be O(10/s). CAS-per-transfer may be ok but bench needed.

maria: Hybrid: CAS only for cross-node transfers; intra-node do local bump + broadcast. Readers check local epoch first, RPC only on mismatch.

sam: Need monotonic epoch + node-id tie-breaker to handle out-of-order broadcasts. Also token TTL so long-lived cursors expire.

jing: Telemetry: prefix_visibility_lag_ms hist, node_observed_epoch gauge, sampled_revalidate counter. Alert if >0.5% reads revalidate or p99 lag >200ms.

devon: I'll bench CAS write latency in staging.

alex: Migration: start telemetry-only, canary broadcast, opt-in CAS, then enforced CAS. Rollback: fallback to broadcast + repair if CAS contention.

maria: Action items: alex -> canary PR with traces; devon -> CAS perf; jing -> telemetry proto; sam -> ops runbook.

sre-bot: Created alert ENG-RUNTIME-PFX-VIS-LAG threshold=200ms p99 scope=production

alex: Good plan. I'll open PR and ping for review.
